name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
summary: Munich's general university, from law and medicine to physics; its bachelor's are taught in German, and its English-taught degrees are master's.

handoff.label: Applying as an international degree student

ib.text: You must pass a recognised German test before a bachelor's. Your IB subjects must meet the KMK rule, and without your final IB certificate you need a recognition letter from Bavaria's ZAST.

apply.via: LMU International Office (form), or MoveIN for some subjects

dates.label: International Office deadline for the winter semester (same date every year)

notes: The Economics BSc is taught mostly in English, but some modules are in German, so LMU requires German for it too.
Subjects with an aptitude assessment need a second, earlier registration with the institute itself, on top of the International Office application.

sources.title: LMU — Applications for admission (International Office; 15 July for the winter semester; "A recognition letter from the Zeugnisanerkennungsstelle für den Freistaat Bayern (ZAST) is required for holders of the International Baccalaureate IB … who have not yet received their final certificate")
